newsitem.title: UK: Alumina market tight, prices to climb - MacQuarie.
newsitem.headline: Alumina market tight, prices to climb - MacQuarie.

text.p: Alumina prices have firmed recently and should extend gains this year as the market has moved into deficit, MacQuarie Equities said on Monday.
Spot prices should climb to $230/50 per tonne, fob Australia, from about $185/90 now and compared to $140/45 when it bottomed out in the third quarter of last year, MacQuarie said in a report.

"The alumina market has swung back into deficit, and with aluminium production continuing to grow and only modest increases in alumina output planned, the market is likely to remain in deficit," the broker said.
Production cuts and improved demand have been behind the run-up in prices.

Aluminum Co of America and Reynolds Metals Co both cut alumina production in the second half of 1996, now having a combined total of two million tonnes per year of idled alumina refining capacity, MacQuarie said.

But a rally of spot prices over the $230/50 level would prompt the start-up of this capacity, especially at Alcoa World-wide Alumina and Chemicals' refineries at Sao Luis, Brazil and Point Comfort in the US, which have recently been expanded, it added.
"At the same time as Alcoa and Reynolds' latest alumina production cuts were beginning to bite, aluminium production, and therefore alumina demand, has been increasing steadily," the report said.
Data from the International Primary Aluminium Institute imply an increase in alumina demand of over 400,000 tonnes in the second half of 1996.
In addition, Chinese imports have increased, with official trade data showing net imports of alumina at 680,000 tonnes in the second half of last year compared with 469,000 tonnes in the first half.
